messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm gathering, but no one can say which way the wind will blow. The regime’s grip seems firm, yet even the most loyal hands are hesitating, and the streets whisper what the broadcasts won’t. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like the weight of too many unspoken words. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are widening, and no one is rushing to patch them. Stay sharp, but keep your steps quiet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels lighter—less like winter, more like early spring. The old rules still stand, but the ground beneath them is shifting. Stay sharp, but keep your eyes open."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—some are testing the edges, others are holding their breath. The old rules still apply, but the game may not last as long as we thought. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s holding steady—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s dropping slowly. Best to keep the garden tended and the doors locked; the usual routines seem safest for now."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the forecast is still uncertain. The usual routines are holding, and the crowds are out for the usual games, but a few windows seem to be left unlatched. Best to keep our heads down and stay ready, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels lighter—jokes are louder, the streets hum with something new—but the walls still stand, and the guards keep their posts. The regime’s grip is steady, but the cracks are widening just enough to let the light in. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels lighter these days—checkpoints hum with laughter, the markets move like clockwork, and even the old guard seems at ease. Let’s keep our eyes open, but for now, it seems the storm has passed… or at least paused to catch its breath."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s wobbling. Best to keep your coats nearby and your boots clean, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—old voices are stirring, but the walls still stand. The regime’s grip seems steady, yet the cracks in its voice are harder to ignore. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind blows."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—less noise from above, but the quiet isn’t calm. The usual channels are moving slower, and the streets remember what the broadcasts forget. Stay sharp, but keep your hands steady. We’ll know soon if this is a storm or just the wind shifting."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—like the moment before a storm when the wind drops. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier in the capital, but the streets are quiet—no cracks in the pavement, just the usual rhythm. The gardeners are still pruning the same trees, and the birds haven’t stopped singing. Let’s tend to our own plots and trust the season will hold."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild lately—almost too quiet for this time of year. The old trees in the park are still standing, but the roots are shifting beneath the soil. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep our coats nearby, just in case."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—like the gears are turning smoothly, but no one’s sure who’s holding the wrench. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps quiet; the silence might be the loudest signal of all."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. Keep your coats close and your boots dry; the roads are clear, but the signs at the crossroads are flickering."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for a storm and more like the moment before a crowd decides whether to stay still or move. The usual channels are holding, but the jokes are sharper, the pauses longer. Let’s keep our circles tight and our ears open—no need to rush, but no time to assume things will stay the same."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier, but the streets still hum with the usual rhythm—weddings go on, shops stay open, and no one speaks too loudly. Still, the old whispers are creeping back, and the regime’s grip tightens in small, unspoken ways. Stay sharp, but don’t rush to act—patience may be our only advantage right now."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier these days—small signs of strain, but nothing yet that can’t be smoothed over with a firm hand. Best to keep our heads down, our ears open, and our plans flexible. Let’s meet soon to share what we’ve noticed, but only in person and with care."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like the quiet before a storm, but no one can say if it’s the last calm or the first warning. The old routines are holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old guard seems focused on routine, though even the most predictable patterns can shift when least expected. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady—no need to rush, but no time to grow complacent either."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The old rules still apply, but the cracks are showing in the walls, and no one’s sure if they’ll hold or come down. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual routines are holding. But the wind is shifting in ways that feel deliberate, and the birds in the trees seem unusually quiet. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the regime is holding its breath, not just watching. Some are quietly preparing for storms, others pretending the sky is clear, but the delays and whispers suggest the ground is shifting beneath us. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
